node-1.label: A 20 × 14-cm² unhealed ulcer on the back has persisted for 3 years

node-2.label: The patient is a 30-year-old woman with a 7.5 × 4-cm² patch of healthy skin on the left forearm lacking blistering

node-3.label: Blood cell genotyping revealed compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1

why.why: The pathologist explicitly states that the RDEB diagnosis is clear based on compound heterozygous COL7A1 splice-site mutations and immunofluorescence/electron microscopy showing type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils. The healthy forearm patch and grafted area with preserved collagen are interpreted as revertant/unaffected skin, further reinforcing RDEB. The only remaining gap, ulcer-margin histopathology, affects secondary SCC surveillance rather than the RDEB diagnosis, so confidence is raised from 0.95 to 0.97.

Expert analyses state that ulcer-margin histopathology for collagen VII and malignant transformation is unavailable, so secondary squamous cell carcinoma cannot be excluded in this 3-year chronic wound. The chronic ulcer and COL7A1-related RDEB confer increased SCC risk, warranting surveillance; however, absence of pathological confirmation keeps confidence moderate, increased only slightly from 0.25 to 0.3.

The pathologist’s analysis reiterates that the compound heterozygous COL7A1 mutations plus the immunofluorescence/electron microscopy findings essentially exclude a chronic non-genetic ulcer. The healthy patch and grafted area are consistent with revertant/unaffected skin in RDEB, not with an alternative non-genetic cause, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.02.
